business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Double Taxation Convention (as amended by 2006/2009 Protocols)
France–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended)
France–China Investment Protection and Double Taxation Treaties (BIT and DTA as updated by 2013/2018 protocols)
EU–France intra-EU investment protection and tax arbitration instruments under EU law

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-50-1; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 5 February 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Décret n° 2021-1019 of 30 July 2021 concerning the Registe des bénéficiaires effectifs; Code de commerce, Articles L. 123-11-2 and R. 123-136; Law n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each non-French shareholder, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry / police authority of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states) followed by certified French sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current corporate registry extract for each non-French corporate shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified French sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office: French lease agreement or approved domiciliation contract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Owner or authorized societé de domiciliation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of signatures may be required; no apostille required for French domestic documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of monetary capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de capital) issued by a French bank or Caisse des Dépôts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution or deposit-taking entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; must be issued in French or with certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of association (statuts) duly signed by all shareholders and, where applicable, notarized where real property is contributed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French legal counsel / notaire if notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed before a non-French notary; otherwise no apostille for French domestic notarial deeds

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 as amended), UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN/BIS lists, French domestic sanctions maintained by TRACFIN and Direction générale du Trésor, and FATF/AMLD5 politically exposed person (PEP) definitions; enhanced due diligence applies where a UBO or close associate is a PEP, with source-of-funds verification and senior management approval required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) for name availability search; official filing portal is Guichet Entreprises (https://www.guichet-entreprises.fr), supported by the greffe du tribunal de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate and registry submissions must be in French; foreign-language documents must be accompanied by apostille/legalization and a sworn French translation. The corporate name must be in characters compatible with the French RCS registry, may be in a foreign language, but must not contain, alone or in translation, words contrary to French public order or creating confusion with protected public designations (Code de commerce, Article L. 123-24).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no formal name reservation; preliminary clearance via Infogreffe remains valid for 30 days before filing. If the greffe rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the President of the Tribunal judiciaire (formerly Tribunal de première instance) or, for commercial matters, to the President of the Tribunal de commerce having jurisdiction over the registered office. The appeal must be filed within 15 days of written rejection, must set out the legal grounds showing non-confusion with existing RCS registrations and non-violation of protected tokens, and is governed by Articles L. 123-1, L. 123-24 and R. 123-128 of the Code de commerce; a court hearing is expedited and a provisional name may be used pending decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for a SAS engaged in automated dropshipping/e-commerce, provided that a domiciliation contract is concluded with an authorized third-party domiciliary agent (société de domiciliation) licensed under Article L. 123-11-2 of the Code de commerce and the registered office is in France; foreign directorship and majority non-resident ownership are permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annualized risk for a compliant e-commerce/dropshipping company; risk rises to 30% where the registered office is purely domiciled with no operating documents, staff, or operational evidence available to tax and registry inspectors. URSSAF, DGFIP, and the Tribunal de commerce may conduct unannounced verification visits upon suspicion of fictitious establishment.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for due diligence and administrative follow-up

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) and Articles R.123-1 et seq. (registration procedures)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) – local registry where the registered office is located
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and Form M0 (déclaration de création d'entreprise) filed via the formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital required; capital is freely determined by shareholders. If capital is contributed in cash, it must be deposited in a French bank account or with a notary (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations) until the company is registered; a certificate of deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) hereby subscribe to the share capital as set forth in the Articles of Association, and that the registered office be established at the address stated therein. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: [Name] as President, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Secretary. The President is authorized to execute all documents necessary for incorporation, to open bank accounts, and to take all actions required to commence operations. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or shareholders directly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts (Articles of Association) in French, including company name, registered office address, corporate purpose (retail sale via automated dropshipping networks), share capital, share classes, and governance rules. All shareholders must sign the document. If a notary is used, the notary will authenticate the signatures and retain a copy.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office (e.g., lease agreement or utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Articles, correct the identified deficiencies and resubmit. Notarization may be required if the Articles are challenged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank or notary (Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the company's name and deposit the subscribed cash capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) from the bank or notary. This certificate is mandatory for registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit is rejected due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing documents and reapply. Ensure the capital amount matches the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement journal (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in an authorized legal gazette, including company name, legal form (SAS), capital, registered office, corporate purpose, and duration. Obtain a copy of the publication (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is delayed, contact the gazette to expedite. Ensure the notice complies with legal requirements to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Grefe du Tribunal de Commerce (via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Form M0 (déclaration de création d'entreprise) online, attaching the signed Articles, capital deposit certificate, legal notice publication, and proof of registered office. Pay the filing fee. The registry will review and issue a Kbis extract (official registration certificate).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registry will issue a notice of incompleteness. Correct the deficiencies and resubmit within the given timeframe. If the application is rejected, appeal to the registry or correct the errors and file anew.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Kbis Extract and Post-Registration Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful registration, the registry issues the Kbis extract (official proof of legal existence). The company must then complete post-registration formalities: register for social security (URSSAF), obtain a SIRET number, and register for VAT if applicable. For dropshipping, no specific industrial license is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed, contact the registry. If post-registration formalities are incomplete, rectify with the relevant authorities (e.g., URSSAF) to avoid penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – retail dropshipping does not require industrial licensing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique (French Ministry of Ecological Transition)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical manufacturing or waste generation; purely commercial activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste handling. If warehousing is used, general waste management regulations apply (Code de l'environnement).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification may be required if the company operates a physical warehouse or office space; otherwise, no specific clearance. For any premises, compliance with workplace safety standards (Code du travail) is mandatory, including electrical safety and emergency exits. If no physical premises are used (pure online dropshipping), these requirements are not triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); portal: impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities without a permanent establishment must appoint an accredited fiscal representative and file a French registration application (Form 1476-SD) with the DGFiP, or use the online 'Création d'entreprise' procedure to obtain a SIREN/SIRET number and an intra-community VAT ID under Article 286 CGI for all taxable operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime; French tax legal unity election (intégration fiscale) is available under Article 223 A CGI and may extend to eligible foreign-owned groups; hybrid mismatch adjustments apply under Articles 212 bis and 212 bis A CGI implementing ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,800 annual turnover for supplies of goods (Article 293 B CGI); EUR 37,500 for services; no threshold for non-established foreign suppliers — immediate VAT registration required; EUR 10,000 union-wide threshold applies to intra-EU distance sales of goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for domestic B2B transactions phased from September 2026, with e-reporting to DGFiP through the Portail Public de Facturation via certified dematerialization platforms (PDPs) and API integration; no real-time fiscal stamping applies to export invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under Article 262-1 CGI; dropshipping supplies shipped from French territory to non-EU customers are eligible provided the exporter holds transport evidence and demonstrates receipt outside the EU. Offshore services supplied to non-EU customers may be zero-rated only when tied to exported goods; purely digital services to non-EU consumers fall under the reverse-charge or OSS schemes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claiming fraudulent export zero-rating triggers retrospective VAT recovery, a bad-faith penalty of 80% of underpaid tax under Article 1737 CGI, applicable interest, and criminal liability under Article 1741 CGI; supporting transport, customs, and payment evidence must be retained for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (central bank of France) acting within the Eurosystem; the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance retains competence for exchange rate policy, financial sanctions, and balance-of-payments statistical oversight. Prudential regulation and AML supervision of credit institutions are exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies full convertibility for both capital and current account operations under EU Treaty provisions and the French Monetary and Financial Code. There are no exchange control authorizations for trade settlements, dividend distributions, or capital movements involving EUR within the EEA. Non-resident owners of a French SAS may freely remit dividends and liquidation proceeds after satisfaction of corporate taxes, dividend withholding tax (30% standard or reduced by treaties), and documentary declaration requirements. Residual frictions arise from AML/KYC obligations, EU comprehensive sanctions, and mandatory statistical declarations to the Banque de France for cross-border payments exceeding reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. A French-resident exporter is permitted to maintain foreign currency accounts with authorized credit institutions and to retain all export earnings offshore, subject to balance-of-payments reporting. French resident entities must, however, provide the Banque de France, via their intermediary bank, with transaction-level data for cross-border funds transfers and must file annual direct investment reports when applicable. Exports to sanctioned jurisdictions are strictly prohibited and subject to DG Trésor controls.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel (CM Group / Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and Operational Account
Operational Account only (no capital escrow services for cross-border e-commerce)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as a secondary treasury gateway, but NOT as the sole primary banking rail. ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto and Treezor, and passport-holders under PSD2 such as Revolut Business, provide rapid remote onboarding, segregated sub-accounts, and multi-currency EUR/USD/GBP account capabilities. They can legally support settlement of operational flows, supplier disbursements, and payment gateway payouts. Critical limitations: EMIs cannot extend credit, issue documentary letters of credit, or hold paid-in share capital in a legally compliant compte bloqué arrangement; for those functions a licensed credit institution is mandatory. Foreign EMIs without an EU passport cannot operate in France and will not satisfy French treasury compliance expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident director of a French SAS, Tier-1 domestic banks de facto require a face-to-face onboarding meeting at the bank's branch or, exceptionally, a video-conference interview combined with notarized identity documents apostilled and translated into French. At least one physical visit is generally unavoidable for the initial corporate account opening, unless the company uses a fintech EMI (remote allowed). The bank will inspect the director's passport, proof of residence, original articles of association (statuts), a valid sentinel certificate of incorporation, and a legalized power of attorney if the signatory is not physically present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments concentrated in high-risk jurisdictions such as mainland China, Hong Kong SAR, or other non-OECD states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Durable supplier agreements with legal entity names and addresses; supplier business licenses from the relevant chamber of commerce; commercial invoices and pro-forma invoices; air/sea waybills or shipment manifests; export customs declarations; screenshots of the marketplace supplier dashboard showing authenticated trader identity; and electronic records of previous payment execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of small-value transactions inconsistent with the company's declared paid-up capital and D&B profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized financial projections validated by an expert-comptable (French statutory auditor); marketplace transaction history showing traffic conversion metrics; operational expenditure budget; monthly treasury reconciliation reports; and an institutional anti-money laundering internal control manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered ownership structure or offshore entity opacity, particularly with non-transparent ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean corporate structure chart; French RCS registration extracts; notarized share register (registre des mouvements de titres); complete UBO declaration filed with the Registre National des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE); notarized ID and proof of residential address of each UBO; source-of-wealth documentation including bank statements reflecting origin of funds used for the French incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback ratios and payment reversal rates from online customers using Stripe/PayPal rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback management policy and team organogram; customer service ticket logs and resolution SLAs; order satisfaction records; documented fulfilment timeline with tracking numbers; and evidence of compliance with PCI-DSS certification for e-commerce operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the registered office (domiciliation) and actual operational server locations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation); cloud hosting contracts (AWS/GCP/Azure data-center agreements); remote working policy for non-resident employees; and detailed operational flowchart demonstrating that automated dropshipping requires no on-site physical inventory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial incorporation of a French SAS, the subscribed share capital must be deposited into a temporarily blocked account (compte bloqué) at a French credit institution in the name of the company in formation. The bank issues a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage de fonds) delivered to the depositary or notary; the funds are released only after the company is registered at the RCS. For subsequent capital increases by a foreign parent, the amount is wire-transferred by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA to the company's dedicated account at the relationship bank, with the instruction explicitly identifying the transaction as an 'Apport en compte-courant d'associé' or 'Augmentation de capital'. The bank requires supporting board resolutions, updated UBO declarations, and proof that the remitting entity is the true legal owner of the funds. All inbound transfers above €10,000 are captured by AML controls and balance-of-payments statistical collection by the Banque de France.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments are executed through SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) using the company's bank or an EMI partner. For recurring mid-value disbursements, a standing bank-file transformation with Straight-Through Processing (STP) can be established. For high-value or two-step drop-shipping arrangements with Chinese or global suppliers, an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (UCP600) with a French advising bank is strongly recommended to mitigate counterparty risk. Payment gateway balances (Stripe, PayPal, Amazon Pay) must be swept daily to the central EUR treasury account via ACH/SEPA payout files; automated reconciliation against supplier invoices and logistics events prevents multi-currency fragmentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts (livraison propre) for firm trade commitments
EUR/CNY deliverable forwards and non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for China-based supplier settlements
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF forwards when handling British or Swiss payment rails
Plain vanilla cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) to hedge medium-term commercial liabilities
Base-plus-option currency collars (risk-reversal structures) permitted for non-speculative hedging of forecasted dropshipping inflows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels: balance sheet, income statement, annexed notes, management report and audit reports when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year close, and no later than one month after shareholder approval; for a 31 December fiscal year, the combined filing deadline is 30 June of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal court injunction, an administrative penalty of €1,500, and potential court-ordered compliance under mandatory enforcement; repeated failure to file can result in administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration (Déclaration de résultats n°2065-SD, including corporate tax (IS/IR) return and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service Impôt des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 30th day of the third month following fiscal close; for a 31 December year end, electronic filing is due by 15 May (the precise DGFiP filing calendar may adjust this date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the entity to a 10% flat penalty on the resulting tax, monthly late interest of 0.20%, reassessment by the administration, and possible criminal penalties after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register update and UBO declaration confirmation (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of every direct or indirect change in ownership control; when no change occurs, the existing register is reviewed and confirmed at the annual shareholder meeting held within six months of year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False declarations, omission of a qualifying beneficial owner, or failure to update the registry can attract criminal fines, a ban on managing a commercial company, and ultimate strike-off of the entity from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business‐premises levy franchise filing (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service Impôt des Entreprises (SIE) attached to the registered-office municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration due annually by 15 May; the tax itself is collectable by 15 December of the same year even if the final tax notice is issued later.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or pay incurs late-payment interest of 0.20% per month plus a 10% penalty; persistent non-compliance may trigger enforced collection, legal lien on bank accounts, or administrative sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A French SAS must appoint a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when at fiscal year end two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total €4,000,000, net turnover €8,000,000, or average of 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory where the SAS directly or indirectly controls another entity or is a consolidated subsidiary of a group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP in compliance with Règlement ANC 2014-03 and the EU Accounting Directive; IFRS is mandatory for consolidated financial statements of a group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the annual shareholders’ meeting, the President or sole shareholder certifies the accuracy of the Register of Beneficial Owners and the share transfer records. Any share transfer that moves a holder above or below 25% of share capital or effective control must be registered in the share ledger and the UBO declaration re-filed at the Greffe within 15 days. In an unchanged ownership year there is no separate government fee.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Movements (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Minutes of Shareholder Decisions (Registre des décisions des associés)
Beneficial Owner Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,200 – 3,500 USD (annual virtual or physical registered-office arrangement plus corporate secretarial platform, depending on service scope and international banking needs)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000 – 15,000 USD for a mid-size SAS if audit thresholds are met; under the legal thresholds audit is optional and the fee for a voluntary review or audit, when requested by lenders or creditors, typically ranges USD 3,000 – 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate under Article 219 CGI)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 10 million; research tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) available for qualifying eligible expenditures; no statutory tax holidays or territorial preferential regimes apply.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward permitted with no statutory year limit; annual utilisation capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess taxable income over that threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa n° 2571-SD (corporate income tax return) filed electronically via the EFI (Espace Professionnel) portal on impots.gouv.fr; additional schedules Cerfa 2572 and 2573 submitted with the same e-filing envelope when applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (single annual return; quarterly corporate income tax instalments due in March, June, September and December of the fiscal year are payable separately).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by midnight of the second business day following 1 May; for any other fiscal year end, the return must be filed within three months of the close of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Détermination du résultat fiscal: net profit or loss before regulatory adjustments and exceptional items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all French-source turnover and expenses; if the SAS is a permanent establishment of a foreign company, attach form 2588 and complete the PE paragraph in the additional sheet.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Restaurations and rattachement des revenus: recapture of prior-year allocations, deductions for export-related tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders must not allocate profits of the SAS to their own domestic tax return; all tax base amounts are reported by the French entity itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and creditable withholding taxes (e.g., CIR, foreign tax credits under tax treaties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders holding a direct interest in the SAS are not allowed to personalise these credits on their own return; credits are solely attributable at the French entity level for corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic surcharge; after a formal notice, the surcharge increases to 40%; for fraudulent intent, 80%. Late payment interest accrues at 0.2% per month for the first 10 days and 0.5% per month thereafter, plus a potential additional 5% penalty for failure to comply with e-filing obligations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-EU corporate shareholders under Article 119 bis CGI; 30% effective for non-resident individuals under the PFU (12.8% plus social contributions); 0% for qualifying EU parent companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (holding at least 10% for two years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; provide the TRC and a signed DTA declaration (Form 5001/5002 as appropriate) to the French paying agent before distribution; if the documentation is provided in time, reduced rate applies at source or a refund is requested from the French tax administration within two years of the distribution date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory domestic withholding tax 25% under Article 182 B CGI, reduced to 0% for EU/EEA recipients under the Interest and Royalties Directive; interest: nil domestic withholding on arm's length debt interest, but 75% withholding or non-deductibility is applied where payments are made to a non-cooperative jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File obligation arises where the French entity or its group has consolidated turnover (excluding VAT) above EUR 400 million, or cross-border controlled transaction volume exceeds EUR 100 million; simplified transfer pricing documentation is required for entities with intra-group transactions above EUR 50 million or total assets exceeding EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) but enforces substance-over-form through Article L64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales (abuse of law) and the beneficial ownership doctrine under tax treaties and EU Directives; a French SAS must demonstrate genuine management, operational control, staff, and premises to support its dropout-shipping model and to access treaty relief or intra-group arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SAS with nominal substance that merely hides the real activity of strips-tapping and automated dropshipping, channelling profits to related parties in tax havens without arm's length remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation of transactions, disallowance of deductions, 80% fraud penalties on reassessed taxable income, publication of sanctions, criminal fine for tax evasion up to EUR 500,000 for legal entities and EUR 250,000 for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers face criminal imprisonment of up to five years (increased for organised evasion), civil joint liability for all unpaid corporate taxes, interest and penalties, as well as travel bans, asset freezes and a prohibition on managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late or non-filing of the statutory corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Cerfa 2571-SD within the statutory deadline despite official notification and recurring reminders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% automatic surcharge; 40% penalty after a mise en demeure remains unfilled; 0.2% to 0.5% monthly late-payment interest; collective assessment may produce an 80% penalty; additional EUR 250 per document penalty for each year of missing accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under Article L267 LPF where the defect demonstrates gross negligence or manoeuver; personal summons to tax authorities, restriction of passport, and a ban from holding public contracts are available enforcement tools.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and suspicious cross-border flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using layered Stripe/PayPal payout routes to conceal discrete payments from illicit dropshipping suppliers or failing to report beneficial ownership of the French SAS to the trade register and tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative freezing of the entity's bank accounts, filing with Tracfin (French financial intelligence unit), seizure of company assets, and criminal fines of EUR 1 million for legal entities engaged in money laundering, increased to EUR 5 million in cases of organised money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face up to ten years imprisonment for organised money laundering, confiscation of personal and corporate property, a travel ban, restriction of civil and professional rights, and an order of restitution for the laundered sums with aggravated fines.
